newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil plans big LPG cargoes from Kaarsto.
newsitem.headline: Statoil plans big LPG cargoes from Kaarsto.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday an expansion of the jetty at the Kaarstoe crude terminal north of Stavanger had been completed.
The extension would allow Statoil to become a global player in supplying liquefied petroleum gases (LPG) and condensate, the company's Status Weekly newsletter said.
"The ability to load vessels up to 110,000 deadweight tonnes means cargoes can be sent to distant markets at competitive rates," it said.
Vessels up to 275 metres long and drawing 13 metres can now berth at the jetty compared with previous dimensions of 210 metres and 12 metres respectively.
Jone Fuglestein, in Statoil's Oil Trading & Supply division, said a 40,000 tonne LPG shipment was due to be transported in early June.
"We're working to ship out 60-80,000 tonnes of condensate in the second half of June, either alone or in combination with crude oil from the Mongstad terminal near Bergen," Fuglestein said.
